page: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is an arm64 compute instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. The instance provides 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs based on the ARMv8 Cortex-A72 architecture clocked at 2.3 GHz. Each core operates with a single execution thread without simultaneous multithreading, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, with no L3 cache present. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB total, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance lacks bundled local storage, relying on external block storage, and includes no GPUs. Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark testing illustrates the limitations of the first-generation Cortex-A72 architecture relative to modern server platforms. In synthetic CPU tests, the instance records average tier results in stress-ng with scores of 1491.99 in single-core and 11904.08 in multi-core routines. However, Geekbench scoring places the instance in lower tiers, yielding a single-core score of 410.0 and a multi-core score of 2143.0. Compilation testing with Clang reaches 3648.0, and PassMark overall CPU performance measures 3170.47. Cryptographic acceleration is limited to standard AES instructions, resulting in lower throughput on extended vector and encryption tests.

Memory and network-oriented throughput show similar entry-level characteristics. Large-block memory bandwidth measures 23.51 GB/sec for uncached reads and 8.88 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, Redis achieves 4.24 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 2.41 GB/sec. Data processing tasks reflect low throughput, with single-threaded gzip compression at 9.83 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 19.83 GB/sec. Small 135M language model prompt processing achieves 103.7 tokens per second.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the a1.2xlarge delivers dedicated physical arm64 cores with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, offering economical compute allocation for lightweight containerized services, microservices, development pipelines, and scale-out web serving environments targeting ARM architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is an arm64 instance powered by a first-generation AWS Graviton processor using the ARMv8 Cortex-A72 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro System, the instance features 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs running at 2.3 GHz, 16.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), and a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. The instance includes no bundled local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the middle tier for stress-ng compute tasks, but lower percentiles for Geekbench, memory write bandwidth, and data compression tests. With hardware-accelerated AES cryptography and dedicated core execution, the a1.2xlarge is technically positioned for lightweight, scale-out ARM workloads such as containerized microservices, development staging environments, and basic web serving where dense CPU allocations are favored over high per-core instructions per cycle.
